is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.l. from Dodowa, Ghana (page 2, 'Mosquito Collections').

reports_target_markers.evidence: Genotyped Vgsc L1014F (L995F) and L1014S (L995S) using HOLA (page 2, 'Selection Experiment' and page 5, Table 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 gives exact genotype counts for L1014F and L1014S across control (N=172: 157 RW/RW, 10 RW/+, 3 RW/RE, 2 +/+) and permethrin-selected groups (N=161: 153 RW/RW, 8 RW/+).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from natural breeding sites in Dodowa, Ghana (05°52.67'N, 000°06.36'W) and reared to adults (page 2, 'Mosquito Collections').

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary research article reporting novel field collections, bioassays, microarray expression, and functional metabolism assays.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections occurred between October and November 2006 (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Routine field collections conducted specifically for this study in late 2006.

supplement.evidence: Target marker genotype numbers and percentages are fully reported in Table 2 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study examined permethrin resistance mechanisms in Anopheles gambiae s.s. from Dodowa, Ghana. A total of 333 female mosquitoes (control and LT50-selected cohorts) were genotyped for Vgsc L1014F and L1014S, showing high frequencies of L1014F (>90% homozygosity), alongside microarray and biochemical analysis demonstrating the overexpression and pyrethroid-metabolising activity of CYP6P3.
